e.etymology: A respelling of the English word chosen, used as a name for a child seen as chosen or set apart, often with a religious sense.
From Greek myron, myrrh or perfumed oil. Myron was the Athenian sculptor of the Discus Thrower, and several early saints carried the name.
namesakes: Myron (ancient Greek sculptor of the Discus Thrower)

e.etymology: From Arabic na'ima, living in comfort and ease, related to na'im, bliss. John Coltrane named his 1959 ballad Naima for his wife. In Finland Naima is an unrelated form of Naomi.

assoc.t: Naima, John Coltrane's jazz ballad

e.meaning: feminine form of Charles, free man
e.etymology: The German and Scandinavian spelling of Caroline, from Latin Carolina, a feminine form of Carolus (Charles), which goes back to Germanic karl, free man.
A modern American combination of the popular Ja- opening with Leah.
An African-American coinage of the late 20th century, a form of Javion and Javon with the sound of Jay at the front.
Hebrew tamir means tall and upright, like the date palm, tamar. A similar Arabic name, from a verb meaning to bear fruit, means fruitful.
namesakes: Tamir Rice (12-year-old killed by Cleveland police in 2014)

assoc.t: Tamir Rice, boy killed by Cleveland police in 2014

e.etymology: In the United States a modern name in the style of Dylan, Kylan and Rylan; some use it as a respelling of Milan, a Slavic name from mil, dear, a spelling popular in France. My Lan is a separate Vietnamese girls' name.

assoc.t: Mylan, generic drug maker behind the EpiPen (now Viatris)

e.meaning: Woden's day, the middle day of the week
e.etymology: The weekday, Old English Wodnesdaeg, day of the god Woden. Charles Addams named Wednesday Addams after the rhyme line Wednesday's child is full of woe, and Netflix's 2022 series Wednesday lifted the name.
namesakes: Wednesday Addams (deadpan daughter of The Addams Family)

assoc.t: Wednesday Addams of The Addams Family
Wednesday, Netflix series starring Jenna Ortega

e.note: People will think of the weekday and of Wednesday Addams before anything else.

e.etymology: A double-l spelling of Axel, the medieval Danish form of the Biblical name Absalom, Hebrew for father of peace.
An African-American name, usually taken as a variant of Imani, the Swahili word for faith, which comes from Arabic iman.
The Hebrew word berakhah, blessing, also the term for a prayer of blessing. It is a traditional girls' name in Orthodox Jewish families.
From Sanskrit navya, which means new or fresh and also praiseworthy. It is a popular modern girls' name in India.
A modern name that rhymes with Jade, Cade and Wade. It can also be a spelling of Arabic Zaid or Zayd, increase or abundance.

assoc.t: Zade Meadows of the dark romance Haunting Adeline

e.etymology: A -yn spelling of Dawson, an English surname meaning son of Daw, a medieval pet form of David. This spelling is given mostly to girls.

e.meaning: independent, one who goes their own way
e.etymology: A spelling of Maverick, from Texas rancher Samuel Maverick, who left his cattle unbranded in the 1840s. A maverick became an unbranded calf, then anyone who goes their own way.

assoc.t: Maverick, Tom Cruise's pilot in Top Gun
Maverik, convenience store and gas station chain
Ford Maverick compact pickup (spelled Maverick)

e.etymology: Two Arabic names written as one: Muhammad, praiseworthy, and Ali, exalted. The one-word form is typical of Central Asian families, especially Uzbek and Tajik ones.

assoc.t: Muhammad Ali, heavyweight boxing champion

e.etymology: A spelling of Neil, the English form of Irish Niall. The Old Irish name is of uncertain meaning; champion and cloud are the usual suggestions.
namesakes: Neal Cassady (Beat figure behind Dean Moriarty in On the Road)
Neal McDonough (actor in Band of Brothers and Yellowstone)

e.meaning: sea fort (as a form of Merlin)
e.etymology: A variant of Merlin, the wizard's name, from Welsh Myrddin, sea fort. Marlin is also the big-game fish, named for its spike-like bill.
namesakes: Marlin Perkins (host of Mutual of Omaha's Wild Kingdom)

assoc.t: marlin, the big-game fish with a spear-like bill
Marlin, Nemo's worried father in Finding Nemo
Miami Marlins baseball team
Marlin Firearms, maker of lever-action rifles

e.etymology: A short form of Joshua, from Hebrew Yehoshua, Yahweh is salvation. The short form has been in use since the 19th century.

assoc.t: to josh, to tease or joke with someone
Josh Cellars wine, labeled simply Josh

e.etymology: From the Norman surname Tyrrell, of uncertain meaning, perhaps a nickname for a stubborn person. In American use it also follows the pattern of Terrell and Darrell.

assoc.t: House Tyrell of Game of Thrones
Tyrell Corporation, the replicant maker in Blade Runner

e.etymology: As a first name, the Yiddish form of Hebrew Meir, one who gives light. Mayer is also a common German surname from Middle High German meier, a steward or tenant farmer.

assoc.t: John Mayer, singer-songwriter and guitarist
Oscar Mayer hot dogs and lunch meats

e.etymology: From Sanskrit ahana, an old Vedic word for the dawn. It is used as a girls' name in India.

e.meaning: friend, ally (as a short form of Dakota)
e.etymology: In American use mostly a short form of Dakota, the Sioux word for friend or ally. Kota is also a Japanese boys' name whose meaning depends on the kanji chosen.

assoc.t: Kota, city in Rajasthan, India

e.etymology: A variant of Callaway, a Norman surname from Caillouet in Normandy, a place named from Old Norman French caillou, pebble.
namesakes: Cab Calloway (bandleader who sang Minnie the Moocher)

assoc.t: Callaway golf clubs (spelled Callaway)
Cab Calloway, jazz bandleader

e.etymology: Greek kairos is the opportune moment, as opposed to chronos, clock time. In the New Testament it is God's appointed time, and Kairos was also the Greek spirit of opportunity.

assoc.t: Kairos, Christian retreat program

e.etymology: From the English word dawn, daybreak. It came into regular use in the 20th century, sometimes for a girl born at dawn, and was at its most popular in the United States around 1970.
namesakes: Dawn Staley (South Carolina basketball coach and Hall of Famer)
Dawn Wells (Mary Ann on Gilligan's Island)
Dawn Summers (Buffy's sister on Buffy the Vampire Slayer)

assoc.t: Dawn dish soap
Dawn, Ash's companion in the Pokemon anime

e.etymology: A pet form of Frederick, from a Germanic name built from words for peace and ruler. It is also used for Alfred and for girls named Frederica.

assoc.t: Freddy Krueger of A Nightmare on Elm Street (Freddy)
Freddy Fazbear of Five Nights at Freddy's (Freddy)
Freddie Mercury, Queen frontman
Freddie Mac, the mortgage finance company

e.etymology: The Spanish form of Stephanie, the feminine of Stephen, from Greek stephanos, a crown or garland.
A pet form of names with a lane sound, such as Elaine, Delaney and Melanie, used as a name in its own right since the late 20th century.
The English word lucky, long a nickname and now given as a name in its own right. It has also served as a pet form of Luke and Lucas.

assoc.t: Lucky Brand, jeans and clothing label
Lucky the Leprechaun, Lucky Charms cereal mascot

e.note: Lucky is also one of the most common names for dogs.

e.etymology: An American respelling of Jacqueline with the -lyn ending. Jacqueline is the French feminine of Jacques (James and Jacob), from Hebrew Yaakov, traditionally read as supplanter.
